pages.title: Three Study Layers
pages.text: $(l)Methods$() define a cultivation route, layer progression, and inheritance gates. $(l)Techniques$() are active abilities bound to seven slots. $(l)Divine arts and secret arts$() are advanced or specialized techniques that still use the same server-side learning, cost, cooldown, and execution checks.

pages.title: Current Corpus
pages.text: The shipped corpus contains $(l)136 methods$() and $(l)747 techniques$(). Methods, techniques, manuals, and layer-unlock matrices use exact cross-referenced identifiers; an unknown display name is never guessed into player progression data.

pages.title: Learning and Binding
pages.text: Learn through manuals, jade slips, sect instruction, or another authoritative source. Learned techniques can be assigned to seven slots. On cast, the server rechecks learning, slot, realm, spiritual power, cooldown, technique-blocking status, target, and executable effect.

pages.title: Dynamic Method Layers
pages.text: Methods no longer share a fixed nine-layer cap. A life skill may remain at one layer, ordinary inheritances use their authored limits, and Changchun Gong and Qingyuan Sword Art can reach thirteen. Each next layer may also carry its own realm band; a failed gate consumes nothing.

pages.title: Advancement Costs
pages.text: Advancement cost follows school and attribute: life skills, alchemy, and appraisal are cheaper; body cultivation sits in the middle; sword, combat, demonic, and ghost methods cost more. Long progressions spread cost across layers, wood or healing trends slightly lower, and fire or thunder trends higher.

pages.title: Technique Runtime
pages.text: All 747 techniques have a resolvable runtime type. Dedicated techniques prefer dedicated implementations; the data-driven resolver handles shape, element, target, range, and base damage for the remainder. Unknown or gated effects fail closed instead of bypassing costs or authority checks.
